items: **Mauryan Empire:** period 4th–2nd BCE; key association Chandragupta Maurya, Ashoka. Reigns of the Mauryan period: Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka.
Dhamma, inscriptions, spread of Buddhism, stupas
**Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus:** Chandragupta defeated Seleucus in 305 BC (Mauryan–Seleucid conflict).
**Chandragupta Maurya** is associated with: Mauryan Empire; Megasthenes; Arthashastra tradition.
**Ashoka** is associated with: Dhamma; Kalinga War; Rock & Pillar Edicts; Buddhist propagation.
**Immediate successor of the Maurya Dynasty:** Shunga Dynasty.

parts.t: Kautilya, Megasthenes and the books on the Mauryas
items: Mauryan polity & economy; one of the oldest political books
Sanskrit drama; Chandragupta Maurya; Chandragupta + Kautilya → overthrow of Nandas
**Kautilya / Chanakya:** political thinker of the Mauryan context; work Arthashastra; associated with Arthashastra and Chandragupta Maurya.
**Kautilya / Chanakya as economist:** ancient Indian economic thought; keyword Arthashastra.
**Megasthenes:** associated with Indica, Chandragupta Maurya and Pataliputra.
**Megasthenes on religion** (period of Chandragupta Maurya): Brahmins + Shramanas.
**Earliest to mention forts in Andhra:** Megasthenes.
**Kalinga War (261 BC / BCE):** Mauryas vs Kalinga; Ashoka vs Kalinga; fought in the 8th year after coronation.
**Why Kalinga:** strategic: eastern sea routes + overseas trade + Deccan routes.
**Result / significance:** turning point in Ashoka's life (Ashoka's transformation); strengthened association with Buddhism + Dhamma.
**Dhamma Policy** (Ashoka): moral/social harmony, welfare and religious tolerance.
**How the inscriptions refer to Ashoka:** generally as Priyadarshi / Piyadasi (Piyadassi) and Devanampiya Piyadasi; Piyadassi / Priyadarshi is the name used in inscriptions.
**Devanampiya / Devanampriya:** title of Ashoka, meaning Beloved of the Gods.
**Personal name "Ashoka"** occurs in: Maski; Gujarra; Nettur; Udagolam.

parts.t: Ashokan inscriptions: classes, sites, language and script
items: **Classification:** 1. Rock inscriptions; 2. Pillar inscriptions; 3. Cave inscriptions.
**Major Rock Edict sites:** Shahbazgarhi; Mansehra; Kalsi; Girnar; Dhauli; Jaugada; Yerragudi; Sopara.
**Brahmi:** script of most Ashokan inscriptions; deciphered by James Prinsep (James Prinsep → Brahmi → Ashokan inscriptions).
**James Prinsep:** first scholar to read Ashoka's edicts.
**Kharosthi:** direction right to left; region North-western India (NW India); major Ashokan examples: Shahbazgarhi; Mansehra.
Concern: animal slaughter / sacrifice. Royal kitchen: gradual reduction and eventual stopping of animal killing.
Mentions Chola; Pandya; Satiyaputta; Keralaputta; Tamraparni / Sri Lanka. Also medical treatment for humans + animals (South India + medical care).
Religious tolerance; respect for different religious sects (religious harmony).
Kalinga War; Ashoka's remorse; shift from military conquest to Dhamma conquest; mentions Greek / Yavana rulers.
**Rock Edict XIII on the Kalinga War:** war in the 8th year after coronation; date 261 BC.
**Contemporaries of Ashoka:** Turamaya/Ptolemy II; Antiochus II; Antigonus Gonatas; Magas; Alexander of Epirus.
**Rummindei / Lumbini Pillar:** ruler Ashoka; place Lumbini; marks the birthplace of Buddha (Rummindei → Lumbini → Buddha's birthplace).
**Ashoka's visit:** after the 20th year of coronation (post-coronation visit); worshipped Buddha's birthplace.
**Concessions at Lumbini:** Bali tax exempted; land revenue reduced from 1/6 to 1/8.
**Bhabru / Bairat:** Ashoka's association with Buddhism; Ashoka's title Piyadasi Raja; associated with King of Magadha.
**Kanganahalli:** place Karnataka, Bhima River; stone portrait of Ashoka + queen; inscription "Ranyo Ashoka", meaning King Ashoka.
**Kalsi Rock Edicts:** place Dehradun, Uttarakhand; associated with Ashokan Rock Edicts.
**Erragudi** (Ashoka): asked teachers to inculcate Dharma in students.

parts.t: Sohgaura and Mahasthan: the famine records
items: **Sohgaura Copper Plate:** place Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh; period Mauryan; described as the earliest known copper plate.
**Sohgaura, contents:** food-grain preservation (storehouses); context famine/crisis; earliest royal famine-related order.
**Mahasthan Inscription:** place Bogura, Bangladesh; concern famine relief.
**Sarnath:** Lion Capital of Ashoka; State Emblem → Sarnath.
**Kanakamuni Stupa** (Niglihawa): enlarged by Ashoka 14 years after coronation.
**Ajivikas:** Ashoka + Dasharatha patronised Ajivikas; Barabar + Nagarjuni Caves are associated with Ajivika monks.

lectures.title: Foreign invasions on India and their impact

items: First ruler stated to have invaded parts of India
Western India; later defeated by Chandragupta II
Gupta period; Skandagupta resisted first invasion
Invaded Delhi during Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah
**Darius-I (522–486 BC):** Persian expansion into parts of NW India: Indus + Punjab + Rajputana.
**First Persian invasion:** Darius I is the first Persian ruler associated with capture of parts of India.
**Herodotus:** work Historica; about Indo-Persian relations; Father of History.
**Indian campaign:** 326 BC (Alexander's invasion of India, 326 BCE), in NW India / Punjab; Alexander left India in 325 BC.
**Battle of Hydaspes (326 BCE):** Alexander vs Porus, in Alexander's Indian campaign; Alexander defeated Porus at the Jhelum (Hydaspes = Jhelum).
Political disunity + superior army + Indian allies
**Dhanananda**, the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, was a contemporary of Alexander (contemporary Magadha ruler; dynasty Nanda).
**Agrammese:** the name by which Greek writers referred to Dhanananda (Dhanananda's Greek name).
**Gold coins:** Indo-Greek rulers introduced the circulation of gold coins in NW India (gold coins popularised in NW India), 2nd century BC.

parts.t: Sakas: Rudradaman and the Junagadh inscription
items: **Sakas / Scythians:** 1st century BCE; Western India; later defeated by Chandragupta II.
**Junagadh inscription:** ruler Rudradaman I; place Girnar / Junagadh, Gujarat; date c. 150 AD; language Sanskrit; script Brahmi; important for Sudarshan Lake.
**Special features:** earliest perfect Sanskrit inscription; early (earliest) specimen of Kavya style.
**Rudradaman-I as patron:** cultural arts + Sanskrit literature.
**Gold : Silver ratio** under the Saka-Kshatrapas: 1 : 35 (important numerical fact).
**Rare coins of Chastana** (Chastana / Karddamaka): copper. Chastana issued silver + copper; copper relatively rare.
**Chandragupta II:** silver Rupaka after Saka victory.
During Skandagupta's reign (Gupta Empire); defeated by Skandagupta
Leader of the second Huna invasion (attack)
**Gwalior inscription:** territory of Mihirakula (Gwalior → Mihirakula / Nagabhata I).
**Muhammad-bin-Qasim:** Arab invasion and conquest of Sindh, 712 AD (711–12 CE).
**Result:** Dahir defeated & killed; Arab expansion remained largely limited (confined) to Sindh & Multan.

parts.t: The Turkish invasions: Mahmud Ghazni and Muhammad Ghori
items: **Mahmud Ghazni (1000–1027):** repeated invasions of India (North India); 17 invasions; objective mainly wealth / plunder; Mathura, Thanesar, Somnath.
**Somnath campaign (1025–26):** Mahmud Ghazni's attack on the famous Somnath temple.
**Al-Biruni** (period of Mahmud of Ghazni): Hindu religion, Puranas, Sanskrit, Yoga.
**Muhammad Ghori:** first attack on India in 1175 CE; against Prithviraj / Jayachandra: Tarain + Chandawar.
**Impact of Ghori's Turkish invasion:** major impact; foundation of Delhi Sultanate.
**Mahmud Ghazni:** silver coins with Arabic + Sanskrit legends.
**Muhammad Ghori:** coins with Lakshmi; some with Arabic Kalma.
